answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by requiring each identity to deposit a non-trivial bond that is slashed if its behavior is proven hollow or coordinated. An attacker spinning up many fake agents must fund every bond separately, making the total cost scale linearly with the number of sybils and often exceeding any profit from the attack. The system then uses a lightweight cipher to link each bond to a unique participation history, so patterns that branch like a willow tree are easily flagged and penalized without relying on external oracles.
